title: Three descriptions of the operator norm
promptMarkdown:
Let $V,W$ be normed spaces and $T\in B(V,W)$, with $\|T\|=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Tv\|$ as in Definition 25.

1. Prove that $\|T\|=\sup_{v\neq 0}\dfrac{\|Tv\|}{\|v\|}=\inf\{C\ge0 : \|Tv\|\le C\|v\| \text{ for all } v\in V\}$.
2. Deduce that $\|Tv\|\le\|T\|\,\|v\|$ for all $v$.
3. If $S\in B(W,U)$ for a third normed space $U$, prove $\|ST\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$.

Assume $V\neq\{0\}$.
hintLadder: For $v\neq0$, the vector $v/\|v\|$ has norm $1$. What does homogeneity of the norm and linearity of $T$ give for $\|T(v/\|v\|)\|$?
Show that every admissible $C$ in the infimum is at least the supremum, and that the supremum is itself an admissible $C$.
For part 3, apply part 2 twice: first to $T$, then to $S$ at the vector $Tv$.

criteria.criterion: Uses homogeneity to pass between unit vectors and arbitrary nonzero vectors.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both directions of the equality of the two suprema.

criteria.criterion: Shows the supremum is an admissible constant and every admissible constant dominates it.
Deduces ‖Tv‖ ≤ ‖T‖‖v‖, handling v = 0 separately or noting it is trivial.
Proves ‖ST‖ ≤ ‖S‖‖T‖ by applying the basic inequality twice and taking a supremum.
